propositions: When a final push is rejected on an ephemeral runner, the Jira rebar-id label persists but local CREATE event and binding are lost, causing the key to become permanently unbound because all healing paths stand down on the label presence.
The L10 guard in binding_walk.py unconditionally skips adopt when a rebar-id label is present, preventing recovery of lost local state after ephemeral runner crash.

Recovery extension in binding_walk.py detects marked-but-unstored keys (rebar-id label equals deterministic inbound local id, no binding store entry, no local ticket) and replays adopt through existing inbound-create leaf instead of standing down.
Idempotent replay keyed on deterministic inbound local id (_jira_key_to_local_id) ensures replayed adopt converges on same local id, binding, and rebar-id label without introducing duplicates.
Foreign markers, multi-marker keys, keys with pending store entries, and retired keys continue to stand down via the conditional _adopt_stands_down helper, preserving L10/L11 double-bind protections.
Bridge fsck unbound_jira audit remains untouched and continues alerting until binding actually exists, providing post-heal verification that recovery succeeded.
